Using its full genomic sequence as a reference, we developed a visual molecular diagnostic assay integrating reverse transcription recombinase polymerase amplification (RT-RPA) and CRISPR/Cas12a collateral cleavage. Single-variable gradient assays were performed to optimize core reaction components, yielding optimal concentrations of 10 nM crRNA, 12.5 nM LbCas12a and 400 nM ssDNA-FQ reporter. The established assay achieved a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.55 copies μL⁻¹, corresponding to a 105-fold higher sensitivity than standard RT-PCR. No cross-reactivity was detected against five prevalent plant viruses: potato virus Y, tobacco vein banding mosaic virus, chilli veinal mottle virus, sugarcane mosaic virus and cucumber mosaic virus. The complete workflow takes less than 1 h, with readouts obtainable via portable UV transilluminators or disposable lateral flow dipsticks (LFDs). Testing of field-collected wisteria leaf samples generated diagnostic results fully concordant with RT-PCR. Overall, our RT-RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a-LFD platform enables sensitive, specific and operationally straightforward point-of-care detection of WVMV for field surveillance.

papers.title: Occurrence of tomato brown rugose fruit virus infecting field tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum ) in Hawaii.
papers.abstract: In this short communication, we describe the occurrence of the emerging tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV, Tobamovirus fructirugosum) in Hawaii. Disease and pathogen surveys conducted across the state focusing primarily on field tomato production reveal the presence of ToBRFV in multiple islands, and consistent detection of the virus for several years at the same field suggests it can persist in the field. To our knowledge, this is not only the first report of ToBRFV in Hawaii, but also the first official report of its presence in commercial field for tomato production in the U.S. Analysis of Sanger sequencing data reveal a high identity (>99.4%) between the detected virus isolates and ToBRFV genome sequences reported in the database. Considering the devastating impact of the virus on tomato production, we will work with growers to identify the source of the virus infection and develop practical management strategies to mitigate its impact.

papers.title: Multiplex TaqMan qPCR assay for the rapid detection of Echinococcus spp. in the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
papers.abstract: The co-endemicity of multiple Echinococcus species poses major challenges for accurate pathogen detection and standardized echinococcosis surveillance and control, particularly on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Nevertheless, conventional molecular detection methods rely on cumbersome conventional and nested polymerase chain reaction (PCR) combinations, which suffer from low detection efficiency, high contamination risks, limited capacity for single-tube multi-species identification, and poor repeatability for low-parasite-load samples, resulting in the absence of standardized, field-applicable detection systems for echinococcosis. To address these limitations, this study developed and validated a novel multiple TaqMan quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) assay based on a lyophilized pre-mixed one-step PCR system for simultaneous identification of three dominant pathogenic Echinococcus species (Echinococcus granulosus s.s., E. multilocularis, and E. shiquicus) in a single reaction. The assay showed excellent analytical performance, including high specificity, excellent linearity, and a low limit of detection of 400 copies/mL. Validation with confirmed samples showed sensitivity of 93.44% and specificity of 100%, significantly superior to conventional combined PCR assays with 67.21% sensitivity. It stably detected trace Echinococcus DNA in complex heterogeneous field samples such as feces from definitive hosts and tiny atypical lesions from intermediate hosts, and accurately identified mixed multi-species infections. Featuring a simplified workflow, low contamination risk, high reproducibility, and suitability for standardization, the developed lyophilized multiplex qPCR system provides a robust technical tool for high-throughput epidemiological surveillance, precise pathogen tracing, and differential diagnosis of echinococcosis in high-altitude endemic regions.

papers.title: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Summit on Genetics in Kidney Health: A United States Perspective.
papers.abstract: Genetic testing and genomics are now essential components of precision kidney care, with the potential to inform diagnosis, management, family planning, and transplant decisions. Expansion of genetic testing is increasingly feasible with continuing improvements in diagnostic yield and variant interpretation as well as declining costs. The Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) Genetics in Kidney Health Summit convened experts in nephrology, genetics, genetic counseling, and related disciplines, together with patients and caregivers, to identify strategies for incorporating genetic testing more fully into kidney care in the United States. Patients and caregivers described genetic testing as a possible means of obtaining clarity about the cause of disease, even when treatment options are limited, and of informing reproductive decisions and cascade testing in at-risk relatives. Reflecting these perspectives, summit participants discussed a shift from criteria-based selection toward a more inclusive testing strategy, reframing the question "who should be tested?" to "who should not be tested?" To avoid exclusion of patients who could benefit from genetic testing, testing strategies should be broad and inclusive, potentially approaching universal testing within key clinical contexts, such as early-onset disease, atypical clinical features, family history of CKD, CKD of unexplained cause, or the presence of extrarenal manifestations. To address the current shortage of experts in nephrogenetics and genetic counselors, collaboration of major American nephrology and genetics organizations is needed to enhance kidney genetics training for both trainees and practicing clinicians. Centers of excellence, which at minimum should include a nephrologist with demonstrated expertise in genetic kidney diseases, at least one genetic counselor, and access to accredited laboratories and bioinformatics, can provide guidance to community nephrologists through telemedicine, virtual case discussions, and shared protocols.

papers.title: Diseases causing nervous signs in cattle in South America.
papers.abstract: Neurological diseases in cattle are among the most important diagnostic challenges in veterinary practice and diagnostic laboratories. In South America, surveillance systems and diagnostic networks have progressively expanded the recognition of diseases causing nervous signs in cattle, yet available information remains fragmented across countries. This review integrates current knowledge on the main diseases causing nervous signs in cattle in South America, with emphasis on their clinical presentation, etiopathogenesis, pathology, and diagnostic relevance, and includes brief information on treatment, control, and prevention. For practical purposes, bovine neurologic disorders are organized according to their etiologic origin into infectious, parasitic, toxic, metabolic, neoplastic, and genetic or congenital. Among infectious conditions, rabies remains the most important viral encephalitis in the region, while bovine herpesviral meningoencephalitis, malignant catarrhal fever, listeriosis, thrombotic meningoencephalitis, and suppurative bacterial infections are also relevant differential diagnoses. Parasitic disorders such as cerebral babesiosis, Trypanosoma vivax infection, nervous coccidiosis, neosporosis, coenurosis, and amoebic meningoencephalitis are less frequent but regionally significant. Toxic and metabolic causes are highly diverse and include plant and fungal intoxications, pesticide and lead poisoning, polioencephalomalacia, hypomagnesemia, vitamin A deficiency, ketosis/fatty liver syndrome, and hypocalcemia. Less common but clinically important conditions include nervous system neoplasms and congenital or hereditary disorders. A single integrated table summarizes, for each condition, the etiologic agent, geographic distribution, affected age group and neurolocalization, main neurological syndrome, principal lesions, field diagnostic aids, samples for laboratory confirmation, laboratory diagnostic methods, and the available treatment and control measures. This review highlights the wide etiologic spectrum of bovine diseases causing nervous signs in South America and emphasizes the importance of a systematic diagnostic approach integrating epidemiology, clinical neurology, gross pathology, histopathology, and targeted ancillary tests. A better understanding of these conditions should improve differential diagnosis, therapeutic decision-making, surveillance, and preventive strategies in cattle production systems across the region.

papers.title: Thermodynamically Guided CRISPR Spacer Optimization: Strategy-Dependent Off-Target Trade-Offs.
papers.abstract: Most CRISPR-Cas9 design tools select guide RNAs (gRNAs) by ranking predefined candidates rather than actively optimizing them. Here we instead formulate SpCas9 spacer refinement as a constrained search problem, in which a limited number of nucleotide substitutions may be introduced outside the PAM-proximal seed region. The search is driven by a thermodynamically grounded objective that combines CRISPRspec-based specificity with penalties for suboptimal GC content and long homopolymer runs. Within this single setting we compare five search strategies: three reinforcement-learning (RL) policies, which are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Quantile-Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN), and Rainbow Deep Q-Network (Rainbow DQN), together with a nonlearning score-guided search and a prompt-guided large language model (LLM). All five share the same objective, mutable positions, substitution budget, and evaluation protocol, so that only the search strategy differs. On 100 held-out IGF2R guides from a gene and chromosome excluded from training, every strategy significantly reduced the predicted off-target burden (38.6-78.3%) and improved independent specificity metrics without degrading on-target scores. The strategies nevertheless differed sharply in per-guide safety: the LLM achieved the largest aggregate reduction but introduced new off-target sites into 38% of guides that were initially free of them, whereas PPO, an on-policy RL algorithm, retained a strong gain with the lowest regression rate of 15%. These results show that the thermodynamic objective supplies a robust common optimization signal, while the choice of search strategy governs the trade-off between aggregate improvement and regression of already-favorable guides.

papers.title: DeepMolVir: Learning Virtual Virus Representations for Sequence-Aware Virus-Inhibitor Activity Prediction.
papers.abstract: The growing threat of emerging and drug-resistant viruses demands efficient approaches for predicting virus-inhibitor interactions. However, most existing computational models treat viruses as categorical identifiers and fail to capture sequence-level biological information. Here, we assembled a data set of 50,711 compound-virus activity pairs spanning 178 viral species and explored protein language models as a strategy for viral representation learning. Using embeddings generated by ESMC-600M, we introduce a virtual virus representation in which viruses are encoded as sequence-derived biological entities rather than as taxonomic labels. These viral representations are integrated with molecular features to model compound-virus interactions. In extensive 5-fold cross-validation, DeepMolVir demonstrated strong predictive performance, achieving an AUC of 0.8653 and an RMSE of 0.9480. Notably, virtual virus representations consistently outperformed conventional taxonomy-based encodings, while ablation studies highlighted viral sequence information as a key contributor to the model performance. Case studies on Nipah virus and hantaviruses further demonstrated the ability of DeepMolVir to identify candidate antiviral scaffolds and support cross-family drug repurposing. Collectively, our findings establish protein-language-model-based viral representation learning as an effective strategy for sequence-aware antiviral activity prediction and provide a foundation for computational antiviral discovery. Code and data are available at GitHub: https://github.com/Sunny-RPX/DeepMolVir.

papers.title: Structural and biochemical insights into infectious bronchitis virus endoribonuclease Nsp15.
papers.abstract: RNA viruses are not only a human health concern but also an economic concern due to animal infections in major industries. Nsp15, a uridine-specific endoribonuclease conserved across vertebrate nidoviruses, processes viral RNA to evade detection by the host immune system. While the enzymatic function is conserved, the oligomeric state necessary for activity does not appear to be strictly conserved across nidoviruses. How oligomerization affects Nsp15 RNA recognition and processing remains understudied. Here, we report the first cryogenic electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) structure of a γ-coronavirus Nsp15, using infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a major poultry pathogen, as a model γ-coronavirus. The structure was determined at 2.4 Å resolution and reveals that IBV Nsp15 adopts the characteristic hexameric architecture observed in α- and β-coronavirus Nsp15, including HCoV-229E, SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, and MHV. To investigate IBV Nsp15 substrate specificity, we performed endoribonuclease assays using diverse RNA substrates. Despite the high degree of conserved structure, we used Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) to show that IBV Nsp15 exhibits distinct substrate preferences for the nucleotide adjacent to the cleavage site, though this preference does appear to be context-dependent when using more complicated substrates. We also demonstrate that, while not essential for catalysis, divalent metal ions enhance endoribonuclease activity. Collectively, these findings establish the structural and functional framework for γ-coronavirus Nsp15 activity, uncover differences in RNA substrate specificity, and highlight conserved and divergent features of Nsp15 across different nidoviruses that could be utilized for the development of new antiviral targets.IMPORTANCEInfectious bronchitis virus (IBV), a γ-coronavirus, is a major poultry pathogen that encodes an endoribonuclease conserved across coronaviruses. While its enzymatic function is conserved, assembly differs across the viral family. Structural studies revealed that the IBV endoribonuclease assembles into a hexameric structure much like other coronaviruses, yet Förster resonance energy transfer assays demonstrated a sequence preference for the nucleotide 5' to the cleaved base that has not been observed with previous homologs. Additionally, we found that metal ions can boost endoribonuclease activity but are not strictly required. These findings establish a structural and biochemical framework of the IBV endoribonuclease and expand our knowledge of the enzyme across coronaviruses.

papers.title: Applying pharmacogenetic results from cancer genomic tests to advance precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Precision oncology has largely centered on somatic tumor alterations that inform treatment selection, while germline pharmacogenetic information remains underused despite its relevance to anticancer drug safety, dosing, and supportive care. As cancer genomic tests increasingly return pharmacogenetic results, providers must be aware of these results and understand how to interpret and apply these findings in routine practice. This minireview describes key considerations for using pharmacogenetic results generated through cancer genomic tests, including the scope of reported pharmacogenes from various cancer genomics laboratory vendors, clinical actionability of the findings, variant or allele coverage, specimen requirements, and integration of results into clinical workflows. Oncology-relevant pharmacogenes such as DPYD, UGT1A1, TPMT/NUDT15, CYP2D6, and HLA-B*57:01 may inform therapy with fluoropyrimidines, irinotecan, thiopurines, tamoxifen, targeted agents, and supportive care medications. However, vendor platforms differ substantially in gene inclusion, variant/allele coverage, ordering processes, specimen needs, and whether results are returned automatically or by request. Thoughtful integration of pharmacogenetic results can help oncology teams prevent toxicity, optimize treatment, and fully leverage genomic testing in precision cancer care.

papers.title: Integrated functional, structural, and clinical analyses resolve NLRC4 variant pathogenicity in autoinflammatory disease.
papers.abstract: NLRC4-associated autoinflammatory disease (NLRC4-AID) is a rare disorder in which variant interpretation remains challenging because of limited functional evidence. We performed the largest systematic functional characterization of NLRC4 variants to date, assessing 27 mosaic and germline variants, including four identified in our patient cohort. NLRC4 variants were evaluated for their ability to induce inflammasome and NF-κB activation in cells expressing inflammasome components. Functional findings were integrated with structural mapping and clinical evidence and interpreted according to American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) criteria. All mosaic variants exhibited constitutive gain-of-function activity, whereas only 10 of the 22 germline variants displayed increased functional activity. Functionally activating variants clustered near the ADP-binding site and within the leucine-rich repeat domain, regions critical for nucleotide sensing and maintenance of the autoinhibited state. Overall, 15 activating variants were identified in 37 patients from 20 unrelated families. Childhood-onset disease was associated with germline variants or high-level mosaicism, whereas adult-onset disease predominated in low-level mosaicism. All currently reported mosaic variants fulfilled ACMG criteria for pathogenicity, whereas germline variants exhibited marked functional heterogeneity. Integrating functional, structural, and clinical evidence improves NLRC4 variant interpretation, refines ACMG classification, and supports genotype-informed diagnosis and clinical management.

papers.title: Pathway-specific control of keratinocyte mitochondrial energetic dysfunction improves epidermal homeostasis in chronic inflammatory dermatoses.
papers.abstract: Chronic inflammatory dermatoses involve barrier disruption and metabolic dysfunction, yet keratinocyte mitochondrial regulation remains unclear. This study proposes a framework restoring mitochondrial homeostasis via pathway-specific modulation of AMPK, mTOR, and ROS cascades. An in silico model using HaCaT and NHEK datasets simulated interventions affecting redox balance and ATP production. Demonstrate that AMPK-mTOR regulation improves bioenergetics, reduces oxidative stress, and enhances keratinocyte proliferation better than conventional anti-inflammatory approaches. The framework successfully achieved ATP levels of 3.79 mol/g protein, reduced ROS to 38.6%, increased AMPK activation to 0.85, enhanced mTOR activity to 3.6 units, improved keratinocyte proliferation to 89.7, and elevated cytokine expression to 75.9 pg/mL. Overall, pathway-specific modulation provides superior long-term epidermal homeostasis by simultaneously targeting cellular metabolism, redox balance, and differentiation pathways, presenting a robust computational foundation for treating chronic inflammatory skin conditions.

papers.title: Genetic Diagnoses in an Adult Cohort of Predominantly Antibody Deficiency in Australia.
papers.abstract: Predominantly antibody deficiencies (PAD) are the most common IEI. Despite advances in genomics, the diagnostic yield in adults remains below 40%, leaving most patients without a molecular diagnosis to guide clinical management. We aimed to define the spectrum of causative genetic variants in adult PAD patients. 112 adult PAD patients were subjected to whole-exome sequencing, alongside collection of clinical data including serum Ig levels and absolute B and T cell counts. The median age of the cohort was 47 years (range 18-72), and 57% were female. Most patients had common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) (58%), followed by hypogammaglobulinemia (20%), agammaglobulinemia (9%), specific antibody deficiency (10%), and IgG subclass deficiency (4%). Reduced serum IgG, IgA, and IgM levels were observed in 61%, 65%, and 46% of patients, respectively, while low B and T cell counts were present in 35% and 29% of patients. Likely causative or candidate variants were identified in 34 patients (30%). Nine of ten agammaglobulinemia patients harboured BTK variants, with a structural variant in SPI1 identified in the remaining patient. Among the remaining patients, variants were predominantly heterozygous (67%), followed by compound heterozygous (21%) and homozygous (13%). Variants most commonly affected genes involved in B cell differentiation and signalling (BTK, NFKB1, PIK3R1, PLCG2, and SYK; 44%), followed by CTLA-4 recycling (CTLA, LRBA; 9%) and TACI receptor (TNFRSF13B; 24%). This first report of an Australian adult PAD cohort demonstrates genetic diagnosis rates consistent with international studies and highlights substantial genetic heterogeneity. Using in-house assays, we are currently functionally validating this diverse array of variants.

papers.title: Determinants of DNA-sequence-based Diagnostic Yield in the CSER Consortium.
papers.abstract: Diagnostic yield from exome and genome sequencing varies widely across studies. It remains unclear how much of this variation reflects patient-level factors (e.g., sex, clinical features, race/ethnicity, genetic ancestry) versus site-level practices such as sequencing modality or variant interpretation workflows. We aimed to quantify the contributions of these factors to diagnostic outcomes across five U.S. clinical sequencing sites. We performed a cross-sectional analysis of 3,008 prenatal, neonatal, and pediatric cases from the NHGRI Clinical Sequencing Evidence-Generating Research (CSER) consortium (2017-2023). Clinical indications spanned neurodevelopmental, neurological, immunological, metabolic, craniofacial, skeletal, cardiac, prenatal, and oncologic presentations. Genetic ancestry was inferred from sequencing data, and variants were interpreted using ACMG/AMP guidelines to classify DNA-based diagnoses. Generalized linear mixed models were used to estimate associations between diagnostic yield and fixed effects (sex, prenatal status, isolated cancer, number of clinical indications, sequencing modality, race/ethnicity, and genetic ancestry), while modeling study site as a random effect to quantify between-site variation. The overall diagnostic yield was 19.0%. Multiple clinical indications (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.80, p<0.001) were associated with higher diagnostic yield, and male sex (OR=0.80, 95% CI 0.66-0.96, p=0.017) and prenatal status (OR=0.63, 95% CI 0.44-0.90, p=0.012) were associated with lower yield. Sequencing modality, race/ethnicity, genetic ancestry, and isolated cancer were not statistically significantly associated with diagnostic outcomes. A model without fixed effects attributed ∼10% of variance in diagnostic yield to between-site differences. After adjusting for covariates, site-level variance decreased to 5.7%, indicating consistent variation across sites not explained by measured patient factors. Across five sites, patient-level clinical features influenced diagnostic yield, but substantial site-level variation remained even after adjustment. Differences in variant interpretation, or case-classification practices may contribute to this residual variability. Further efforts to increase consistency in exome- and genome-sequencing diagnostic workflows may help reduce inter-site differences.

papers.title: Bioinspired Membrane Fusion-Gated Hydrogel Biosensor for Extraction-Free Viral RNA Detection of Infectious Influenza Virus.
papers.abstract: Emerging infectious diseases driven by zoonotic spillover demand rapid and reliable molecular diagnostics for pathogen identification and surveillance. However, conventional nucleic acid diagnostics cannot distinguish infectious virions from nonviable RNA fragments, limiting infectivity-resolved virus identification. Here, we report a bioinspired membrane-coated hydrogel (Memgel) sensor that enables extraction-free molecular detection of influenza virus while distinguishing fusion-competent virions from noninfectious viral material. The platform integrates a cell-mimetic supported lipid bilayer with a polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) hydrogel matrix encapsulating recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) reagents. Under endosome-mimicking acidic conditions, hemagglutinin-mediated membrane fusion selectively delivers viral genomic RNA from infectious virions into the hydrogel matrix, triggering sequence-specific amplification while suppressing signals from free viral RNA fragments. As a proof of concept, the Memgel sensor was evaluated for the detection of influenza A (H9N2) in simulated nasal fluid and raw milk matrices, achieving a limit of detection of 10 1.23 TCID 50 mL - 1 while maintaining robust detection performance without RNA extraction. Coupled with a portable fluorescence reader, the system demonstrates compatibility with compact fluorescence-based readout for future point-of-care implementation. This fusion-gated sensing strategy provides a materials-based framework for infectivity-resolved molecular diagnostics of emerging viral pathogens.

papers.title: The Therapeutic Pipeline: Future Treatments and Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: Rare interstitial lung diseases (ILDs) represent a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by various pathogenic mechanisms, clinical presentations, prognoses, and therapeutic challenges. Among these, acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD), pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP), and pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis (PLCH) exemplify rare pulmonary diseases driven by distinct biological mechanisms, including lysosomal dysfunction, impaired surfactant homeostasis, and activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPK) pathways. Recent advancements in molecular biology, genomics, and translational research boosted the development of precision medicine strategies and disease-specific therapies for these conditions. This narrative review was conducted in accordance with the SANRA guidelines. A thorough literature search of the PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus databases was performed from January 2000 to June 2026. Significant progress has been made in treating all three diseases. In ASMD, enzyme replacement therapy with olipudase alfa has greatly improved visceral and lung symptoms, while research in gene therapy, gene editing, and metabolic treatments is ongoing. For PAP, inhaled granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) is now the primary disease-specific treatment, now supported by phase III trial evidence for inhaled molgramostim, complemented by potential therapies such as immunomodulation, macrophage transplantation, and gene-based strategies. In PLCH, the discovery of recurrent MAPK pathway variants has supported the use of genotype-targeted treatments with B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine (BRAF)/threonine kinase and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK) kinase inhibitors. Under these conditions, advances in molecular diagnostics, circulating biomarkers, quantitative high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT), radiomics, and artificial intelligence (AI) are poised to enhance diagnosis, patient stratification, prognosis, and treatment decisions. ASMD, PAP, and PLCH are entering into an era of precision medicine, in which disease-specific molecular mechanisms play an increasing role in guiding diagnosis and treatment. Ongoing integration of genomics, biomarkers, advanced imaging, AI, and targeted therapies could revolutionize the management of conditions such as ASMD, PAP, and PLCH, leading to better long-term patient outcomes.

papers.title: Evolving roles within the genomic medicine workforce: a revised framework for UK practice-position on behalf of the Association of Genetic Nurses and Counsellors and the Clinical Genetics Society.
Non-invasive detection of tissue clonal mosaicism in chronic disease
papers.abstract: Liquid biopsy has transformed our ability to non-invasively interrogate the somatic genome, but its reach has been largely confined to fetal genetics in prenatal testing and tumor genetics in cancer. Clonal mosaicism (CM) pervades non-malignant solid tissues, where somatic driver mutations expand under specific selective pressures and may shape the course of chronic illness. Access to this biology has been limited to invasive tissue biopsies, restricting the field to small cohorts and single time points, and has precluded large-scale, clinically-linked analyses. Here, ultra-sensitive cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing of patients with chronic liver disease revealed genome-wide somatic variants from matched liver biopsies at plasma fractions comparable to those of cancers (10^-4 - 10^-5), with signal corresponding to variants from spatially and phylogenetically related clones. A biopsy-naive targeted panel detected pathogenic variants in chronic liver disease driver genes in 81.5% patients with chronic liver disease, undetectable in controls, with stage-specific enrichment of ACVR2A in early disease and clearance of liver-derived signal following transplant. Extending the framework to inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), we detect clonal expansions of IBD driver genes in active ulcerative colitis, and observe greater detection in patients with pancolitis versus more localized disease. Together, these results open a new domain for cfDNA genetics beyond cancer and prenatal genetics, the non-invasive interrogation of somatic evolution in chronic disease, and establish a framework for the large-cohort, longitudinal, clinically linked studies of solid-tissue CM that has been inaccessible to the field.

papers.title: Machine learning prediction of antimicrobial resistance in respiratory metagenomes
papers.abstract: Background: Targeted therapy for patients with suspected respiratory infections traditionally requires bacterial culture followed by phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), a process that can take up to 5 days. In acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), delays in identifying the causative pathogen and its resistance profile may be especially harmful because patients are critically ill and often receive broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics. The growing burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) further complicates clinical decision-making by reducing effective treatment options and increasing the risk of inadequate initial therapy. Culture-free, AI-driven computational metagenomic strategies have the potential to drastically shorten this window, enabling more rapid targeted therapy prescription. To show the feasibility of such approaches, we develop a proof-of-concept framework based on clinical metagenomics. Methods: We simulated respiratory metagenomes using real-world bacterial genomes with associated antimicrobial susceptibility phenotypes. Each simulated metagenome contained a fixed commensal background and one clinically important respiratory pathogen, Acinetobacter baumannii, Klebsiella pneumoniae, or Pseudomonas aeruginosa, at 5% or 10% bacterial read abundance. Realistic reads were simulated for Oxford Nanopore, PacBio, and Illumina sequencing platforms. Random Forest (RF) classifiers were trained and evaluated using five-fold, strain-grouped cross-validation with fold-specific {chi}2-ranked 13-mer features. ResFinder and KARGA were included as reference-based metagenomics benchmarks and evaluated using the same five held-out folds across the three sequencing platforms and two pathogen-abundance conditions. Results: RF performance varied substantially across species, antibiotics, and sequencing platforms. The strongest and most consistent results were observed for K. pneumoniae, with accuracy reaching approximately 0.96 for ceftazidime, 0.93 for amikacin, and 0.92 for ciprofloxacin. Performance for P. aeruginosa was more heterogeneous: long-read models performed well for amikacin, reaching 0.89 with PacBio and 0.88 with Nanopore, whereas Illumina performed substantially better for ciprofloxacin, ceftazidime, and levofloxacin, reaching accuracies of approximately 0.87, 0.77, and 0.70, respectively. Across most organism-antibiotic combinations, RF accuracy was numerically higher than the classification accuracies obtained with KARGA and ResFinder, which generally remained near 0.50. Increasing pathogen abundance from 5% to 10% and increasing the number of selected features from 2,500 to 5,000 generally produced modest improvements in classification accuracy, although the magnitude of improvement varied across organism-antibiotic combinations and sequencing platforms. Conclusions: Genome-wide k-mer machine learning can recover phenotype-associated antimicrobial resistance signals from simulated respiratory metagenomes, although performance depends strongly on the organism, antibiotic, and sequencing platform. These results represent a simulation-based proof of concept.

papers.title: A2Holo: Dual-Stream Flow Matching of 3D Structure and a Protein Language Model for Conformational Transition Prediction
papers.abstract: Modelling a ligand-bound holo conformation from a ligand-free apo conformation is essential in structure-based drug discovery. We present A2Holo, which casts apo-to-holo prediction as flow matching between two experimental structures rather than generation from noise. It transplants the dual-stream joint attention of in-context image generation to residue-aligned protein language model embeddings and structure. Without ligand conditioning or stochastic sampling, A2Holo's single deterministic trajectory reaches a median C RMSD of 0.809 [A] on the D3PM benchmark, the lowest among existing methods. Its TM-score exceeds even the best of 10 samples from every stochastic baseline on at least 144 of 150 pairs. Beyond performance, we directly measure the transplanted multimodal mechanism itself. Because sequence and structure are residue-aligned, its joint attention can be measured at residue resolution and tested for reproducibility across independently trained model variants. Within the structure stream, the attention a residue receives recovers moving residues better than the attention it emits, and this asymmetry is learned. A2Holo demonstrates a successful multimodal transplant from in-context image generation to protein conformational change, with strong deterministic apo-to-holo prediction. It also provides a quantitative account of how that mechanism organises residue-aligned sequence and structure around the residues that move.

papers.title: aureoRNA enables the interactive, genome-wide analysis of Staphylococcus aureus small RNA targetomes and uncovers new regulatory functions
papers.abstract: Small RNAs (sRNAs) control key steps of infection and stress acclimation in the opportunistic pathogen Staphylococcus aureus. Yet most of the more than 250 annotated candidates remain uncharacterized, and even the best-studied have incomplete target spectra. Here we present aureoRNA, an interactive tool that assembles for each sRNA comparative target predictions, available MAPS interactomes, sRNA-mRNA expression correlation across curated public transcriptomes and placement in groups of independently regulated genes (iModulons), and makes these data explorable in one place. GO- and KEGG-based enrichments summarize the datasets at the pathway level for every sRNA, and a weighted rank product combines available data into prioritized target candidate lists. We generated a new MAPS interactome for RsaD and experimentally validated predictions for three sRNAs: new RsaD targets in threonine and arginine catabolism, citZ as an RsaE target, and prophage genes repressed by RNAIII. aureoRNA is a hypothesis-generating resource for the systematic characterization of the sRNA repertoire of this pathogen.

papers.title: The IGVF Catalog Knowledge Graph
papers.abstract: The Impact of Genomic Variation on Function (IGVF) consortium is systematically characterizing how genomic variation influences regulatory elements, gene expression, and human phenotypes through thousands of experimental mapping and perturbation datasets alongside predictive models. To synthesize these diverse results into quantitative relationships and situate them within established biological knowledge, we developed the IGVF Catalog, a large-scale knowledge graph. Implemented in ArangoDB using schema-validated JSON records. Version 1.3 encompasses nearly 3 billion nodes across 14 entity types (including variants, coding variants, genomic elements, genes, transcripts, proteins, pathways, and ontology graphs for biosamples and phenotypes) connected by more than 8.6 billion edges across 31 relationship types. Edges encode statistical significance, effect sizes, source provenance, and biological context via ontology-linked hyperedges. The Catalog integrates 657 IGVF datasets spanning non-coding reporter and CRISPR perturbation screens (MPRA, STARR-seq, Perturb-seq), coding variant assays (VAMP-seq, SGE, MAVE, DUAL-IPA), and predictive models (scE2G, SEMVAR, cV2F, TLAND, and BlueSTARR), unified with extensive public context including GENCODE annotations, FAVOR and dbSNP variants, TopLD linkage disequilibrium, GWAS, QTLs, and protein interactions. Users can interrogate the Catalog through a web portal (https://igvf.catalog.org) Python and R clients, an OpenAPI-documented API featuring 86 endpoints supporting identifier and genomic-region queries, and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enabling agent-assisted querying with large language models. We demonstrate the Catalog's utility for mechanistic interpretation across three case studies: resolving a FOXA1-dependent enhancer variant (rs11257655) regulating CAMK1D at a type 2 diabetes locus, distinguishing coding (GCKR rs1260326) and regulatory (HNF1A rs1169289) mechanisms for liver traits, and linking vascular CRISPRi-perturbed elements to CDKN2A/CDKN2B and NOS3 in coronary artery disease. Updated quarterly with open data and software, the IGVF Catalog provides a scalable resource for variant-to-function discovery.

papers.title: Deciphering state bridges via a single-cell large language model
papers.abstract: Large-scale single-cell transcriptomic data provide a new avenue for precision medicine by uncovering cellular heterogeneity. However, systematic comparison of remodeling patterns across various biological states remains unavailable. Here, we first developed a computational framework based on a foundation model of single cell biology, Universal Cell Embedding (UCE), to harmonize annotations comprising 36 cell types. Based on an integrated dataset of single cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with 8,789 human samples comprising more than 59 million cells or nuclei across 614 biological states, we then embedded each state with a 36-dimensional vector in a unified space of cell-composition change and further deciphered states bridges by analyzing the relationships among the 614 state vectors. As a result, 22,161 significant bridges (P < 0.05) between the 614 states were revealed. Moreover, we successfully identified a number of well-known bridges such as bridge between Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease (P = 2.21e-15), suggesting the effectiveness of the proposed framework. More importantly, we uncovered a number of new bridges. Furthermore, analyses of the number of changed cell types (NCC) and Shannon entropy revealed heterogeneous and tissue-dependent patterns of cellular composition remodeling. This study provides a new strategy for identifying disease associations and potential therapeutic relationships by deciphering bridges between biological states from scRNA-seq landscape.

papers.title: Genomic foundation models and complementary variant-scoring strategies in LGMD-associated genes: architecture, adaptation, and sequence context
papers.abstract: Genomic foundation models learn representations from DNA sequence, although their usefulness for variant classification depends on the architecture and downstream evaluation procedure. We compared six genomic foundation models using 6,960 ClinVar single-nucleotide variants from ten limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD)-associated genes, with 4,866 variants assigned to training and 2,094 to held-out testing. The analyses included frozen alternate-minus-reference embeddings at 101, 201 and 501 bp, supervised adaptation at 101 bp, and gene-held-out downstream classifier training. GPN-Star V100 and AlphaGenome Atlas AVI were evaluated separately using their native scores. At 101 bp, frozen Evo2 achieved the highest discrimination among the six foundation models (MCC 0.644; AUROC 0.879; AUPRC 0.818). Supervised adaptation increased MCC for three architectures and reduced it for the remaining three. Extending sequence context to 501 bp improved all three primary metrics in five of six frozen architectures, with Evo2 reaching an MCC of 0.864, AUROC of 0.964 and AUPRC of 0.952. Evo2 also led the frozen gene-held-out readouts (pooled MCC 0.641; AUROC 0.852; AUPRC 0.789). GPN-Star V100 and AVI achieved MCC values of 0.929 and 0.938, respectively, using distinct biological inputs and scoring procedures. The number of variants misclassified across all evaluated configurations decreased from five under the original 101-bp readouts to one after including longer contexts and native scores. An exploratory HGVS-category control identified substantial annotation-associated structure in the benchmark labels. The findings characterize classification performance against aggregate ClinVar labels within LGMD-associated genes. Disease-specific pathogenicity and clinical diagnostic utility remain untested.

papers.title: MAPLE: A hierarchical Multimodal Assistant for Pathology vision-Language Evaluation using logic and reasoning
papers.abstract: Pathological diagnosis requires integration of cellular morphology, tissue architecture, and clinical context across gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs), yet existing vision-language models remain constrained to patch-based analysis with resource-intensive architectures unsuitable for routine clinical deployment. Here we introduce MAPLE, a hierarchical pathology vision-language model that performs whole-slide diagnosis and report generation through efficient multi-scale reasoning. MAPLE employs AgenTile, a small 10-million-parameter vision transformer for cellular-level triage at 40x resolution, achieving segmentation performance equivalent to ~65-fold larger models (e.g., CellViT++) while providing ~95-fold faster inference. Cross-magnification integration with a CLIP-based image encoder at 10x and 5x enables recursive selection of the most diagnostically informative regions per slide. On the PathMMU benchmark (7691 image-question pairs), MAPLE's multimodal (image and text) reasoning module is the first to exceed pathologist performance across all four diagnostic domains (PubMed, EduContent, SocialPath, and Atlas), achieving 70.6-81.2% accuracy versus 68.3-72.9% for pathologists. MAPLE demonstrates calibrated clinical reasoning, appropriately expressing uncertainty for metastatic carcinoma requiring ancillary testing while providing a confident diagnosis for benign hamartoma. These results were validated using an additional clinical cohort. Taken together, our findings establish MAPLE as a computationally efficient, clinically deployable system for AI-augmented pathology, particularly suited to resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Integrating CRISPRi perturbation responses and transcription-factor binding priors for regulatory network inference in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype that lacks actionable cell-surface receptors, restricting frontline systemic management to cytotoxic chemotherapy. While recent functional epigenomics shows that TNBC progression is governed by non-coding regulatory remodeling at distal super-enhancers, conventional Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) inference methods rely on observational transcriptomic co-expression, which suffers from technical dropouts and confounding correlations that inflate false discoveries (>30%). Here, we present an interventional network inference framework that integrates large-scale single-cell CRISPR-interference perturbation sequencing (Perturb-seq; GSE224986, 95,678 cells across 11,975 sgRNAs) with ENCODE Factorbook ChIP-seq physical transcription factor binding priors across 819 somatic mutation-associated enhancer loci in human TNBC (MDA-MB-231). Our pipeline reconstructed a tripartite network yielding 5,935 physical TF-enhancer edges, 383,757 functional enhancer-gene edges, and 542,760 unique TF-target gene functional pairs across 372 active enhancers. Topological centrality prioritized master transcriptional drivers governing TNBC oncogenic signaling, including CTCF, POLR2A, EP300, JUND, MYC, and FOS, which regulate Hallmark programs for Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition (p = 1.2 x 10-9) and cell cycle progression. Explainable machine learning (SHAP TreeExplainer) revealed non-linear, thresholded transactivation dynamics for AP-1 and MYC. Quantitative benchmarking against held-out CRISPRi ground truth demonstrated strong discriminatory accuracy (AUROC = 0.8999, AUPRC = 0.8745, Precision = 90.13%, FDR = 9.87%), substantially outperforming GENIE3 (AUPRC = 0.6323, FDR = 35.73%) and co-expression correlation (AUPRC = 0.6814). In silico-simulated driver feature silencing correlated with experimental responses (R2 = 0.473, p < 10-122), and master driver signatures significantly stratified overall survival in the METABRIC (n = 320) and TCGA-BRCA (n = 160; p [≤] 0.019) cohorts. Finally, in silico perturbation modeling indicated that multi-target epigenetic combinations achieved 93% topological disruption of oncogenic regulatory connectivity, nominating prioritized candidate circuits for experimental validation.

papers.title: Vir2vec: A Genome-Wide Viral Embedding
papers.abstract: Genomic language models (gLMs) enable the extraction of meaningful numerical representations from DNA sequences, yet existing approaches primarily focus on human genomes or limited viral datasets, and systematic evaluations of viral representations remain scarce. Here, we introduce Vir2vec, a family of decoder-only gLMs (from 17M to 422M parameters) continually pretrained on a curated viral corpus comprising 565,747 complete genomes and genomic segment records assigned to 295 different species. We also present the viral Genome Understanding Evaluation (vGUE), a seven-task evaluation suite assessing viral representations across broad organism discrimination, evolutionary signatures, intra-genus species classification, variant subtyping, and host-associated phenotypes. Evaluated as a frozen feature extractor under nested cross-validation, Vir2vec achieves the highest balanced accuracy on three of seven tasks (full-genome virus detection, DNA-versus-RNA classification, and host-category prediction) and shares the highest performance on HIV-1 versus HIV-2 classification, while alternative models lead on the remaining three tasks. Taxonomic exclusion experiments further assess generalization of classification capabilities when an RNA-virus clade is excluded from pretraining at species and family levels. Finally, we introduce an argmax-routed SHAP explainability framework that maps feature attributions to codon-level sequence coordinates, highlighting receptor-binding-domain positions associated with SARS-CoV-2 human-versus-mouse host specificity discrimination. Together, Vir2vec and vGUE provide resources for advancing viral genomic representation learning and its systematic evaluation.

papers.title: A transcriptomic-driven segmentation and cell simulation framework for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics and cell-cell communication
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics platforms, such as Visium HD and Atera, enable transcriptome-wide profiling at near-single-cell resolution. However, accurate cell segmentation to define spatial boundaries relies heavily on histological images. Previous approaches struggle in tissues with high cell density, inflammation, or mineralization, leading to transcriptomic bleed-through and inaccurate clustering. To address this, we developed TENGU (Transcript-signal Enrichment and Grouping Unit), a comprehensive end-to-end bioinformatic software package. Unlike existing tools, TENGU employs a transcript-first segmentation approach, prioritizing transcript-signal density as the primary modality and utilizing histological images only as a secondary supplement in unresolved regions. These initial boundaries are further optimized through a transcriptomic-driven cell simulation algorithm that iteratively refines boundaries based on localized gene expression probabilities, effectively minimizing spatial scattering and preserving biologically distinct molecular signatures. The pipeline seamlessly integrates tissue segmentation, high-resolution cell-type annotation, and spatially aware cell-cell communication (CCC) analysis. We rigorously benchmarked TENGU against the 10x Genomics and Bin2cell pipelines for segmentation, and against CellNEST for spatial CCC inference, across diverse and technically challenging microenvironments. TENGU demonstrated superior transcriptomic distinctness in the murine brain and successfully captured matrix-embedded osteocytes in decalcified bone. In murine osteomyelitis, TENGU outperformed CellNEST in sensitivity, localizing both reactive bone remodeling (Tgfb) and dense, abscess-encapsulating inflammatory (Il1a/Il1) networks. TENGU also resolved species-specific pro-tumorigenic hubs (MDK-SDC4) in a human colorectal cancer xenograft and generalized effectively to the Atera platform, delineating CXCL12-CXCR4 and LGALS3-TGFBR2 signaling within highly compacted human breast cancer tissue. By mitigating image-dependent constraints, TENGU provides a highly adaptable, robust computational framework to decode the functional micro-anatomy of healthy and pathological tissues.

papers.title: GlycanPUG: WURCS-Based Heterogeneous Graph Pretraining for Structurally Ambiguous Glycans
papers.abstract: Background: Glycans orchestrate diverse biological processes, yet they remain underrepresented in computational biology compared to proteins and nucleic acids. Although WURCS 2.0 provides a machine-readable structural representation that preserves uncertainty, the evaluated IUPAC-based deterministic workflow processes 43.1% of the GlyCosmos-derived cohort examined here, motivating approaches that retain structural ambiguity. Methods: To overcome this limitation, GlycanPUG (Probabilistic Uncertainty-aware Graph) was introduced as a pretrained graph model for glycan representation learning. By leveraging WURCS 2.0, GlycanPUG represents candidate linkages and substituent attachments using weighted edges and uncertainty attributes within a heterogeneous graph framework. A 4-layer Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with a dedicated node pre-enhancement module aggregates edge features weighted by the assigned edge weights, enabling representation of supported structurally ambiguous glycans without selecting a single resolved structure. The model is pretrained on a preprocessed subset of the GlyTouCan1 repository, which contained 253,596 entries before filtering. After excluding entries linked to downstream tasks and applying sequential structural filtering, 167,020 samples remained and were used for pretraining. Pretraining comprised nine self-supervised tasks. Results: Benchmarking on the GlycanML dataset demonstrates that GlycanPUG shows competitive performance relative to GlycanGT across multi-label taxonomy classification and binary immunogenicity prediction. Crucially, on datasets natively containing structural uncertainties (GlyCosmos, GlyConnect), GlycanPUG effectively processes additional structurally ambiguous entries, achieving 83.5% processable coverage across all glycans from all biological sources in GlyCosmos, with taxonomic classification performance (e.g., mean macro F1 of 0.7376 for Domain). Ablation of the node pre-enhancement module reduces macro F1, and post-hoc analysis identifies rank-dependent associations between structural uncertainty and prediction errors. All results reported above are averaged over ten independent random seeds (1-10). Conclusions: GlycanPUG broadens the set of glycans that can be represented while retaining supported structural ambiguities.

papers.title: Deciphering Molecular Language for Spectral Interpretation with a Foundation Model Pretrained on Repository-Wide Metabolomics Data
papers.abstract: In-depth, scalable structural interpretation of tandem mass spectra from diverse biological tissues and environmental samples is essential for understanding the molecular diversity of cellular environments and the metabolic architecture of living systems. Although community-driven resources such as GNPS and MassIVE have aggregated massive volumes of tandem mass spectra spanning a wide range of organisms, clinical cohorts and environmental surveys, modeling and interpreting this exponentially expanding spectral corpus to distill molecular information and derive meaningful biological insights poses a fundamental challenge for established computational methods. Here we present UltraMS, a dual-polarity foundation model tailored to decipher the molecular language latent in tandem mass spectra through large-scale pretraining on more than 160 million spectra encompassing both positive and negative ion modes. Our findings illustrate that UltraMS is capable of effectively decoding the chemical semantics of molecules underlying mass spectra via self-supervised learning, achieving superior performance across a variety of downstream tasks, including elemental detection, molecular identification, molecular property profiling, and metabolic landscape characterization. Remarkably, UltraMS enables conducting molecular identification with fine-grained spectral interpretability, simultaneously elucidating molecular structures from untargeted MS/MS spectra and providing peak-by-peak substructural attributions via annotation transfer. Deployed on a clinical cohort of human plaque samples, UltraMS demonstrates significant potential in discovering previously unrecognized phenotype-linked metabolites supported by structurally grounded fragment-ion formation pathways, while effectively correcting likely misannotated clinical markers. Furthermore, building on the structure-aware spectral representations learned by UltraMS, we construct UltraAtlas, a chemical-property-resolved map that organizes millions of experimental spectra into a unified coordinate system, enabling millisecond-scale molecular profiling and offering practical guidance for exploratory navigation across vast chemical space. Applied to human scalp metabolomics, UltraAtlas effectively captures distinct metabolic variations across individuals, highlighting phenotype-specific chemical signatures while shedding light on the chemical niches of the resident microbiome. Together, UltraMS and UltraAtlas constitute a generalizable framework for structural elucidation and biological discovery from tandem mass spectra, empowering the comprehensive exploration of the largely undeciphered metabolomes across different domains of life.

papers.title: EM-Claw: An Experience-Grounded Language-Model Agent for Auto Cryo-EM Single-Particle Analysis
papers.abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) processing remains strongly dependent on expert judgement because difficult specimens often require dataset-specific strategies that cannot be captured by a fixed pipeline. Here we present EM-Claw, an experience-grounded multi-agent system for adaptive cryo-EM single-particle analysis. Rather than following a predefined workflow, EM-Claw retrieves processing precedents from previously solved datasets, consults external guidance, proposes and independently evaluates alternative strategies, executes CryoSPARC or RELION jobs, and revises the processing route according to quantitative and visual evidence. Human expertise can be introduced at any stage through natural-language instructions, while successful decisions and processing trajectories are retained as reusable experience. We evaluated EM-Claw on both publicly available cryo-EM datasets and experimental datasets collected in our laboratory, spanning soluble proteins, membrane proteins, GPCR complexes and small transporter monomers. Across these cases, EM-Claw adapted its processing strategies to specimen-specific challenges, including compositional heterogeneity, complex flexibility, preferred orientation and weak particle features. It produced reconstructions at higher resolution than previously published results (0.1~1.3 angstroms improvement) or solved structures that are now being prepared for publication, with no or little human intervention, thereby substantially reducing the time, effort and field experience required for human decision-making.

papers.title: A hidden mitotic vulnerability emerges from BCAT1 redox-motif disruption in Ewing sarcoma
papers.abstract: Cancer cells must keep oxidative stress and chromosome-segregation errors within tolerable limits to sustain rapid proliferation. Because redox homeostasis supports faithful chromosome segregation, disrupting redox-dependent mitotic safeguards could drive chromosomal instability (CIN) beyond cell tolerance and suppress tumor growth. Here, we investigated whether selectively disrupting redox-dependent safeguards could uncouple oxidative-stress adaptation from faithful chromosome segregation, exposing a therapeutic vulnerability at the interface of metabolic regulation and genome maintenance. We used Ewing sarcoma (EwS) as a model because it combines low genomic complexity with elevated oxidative stress and limited redox-buffering capacity. A survival analysis of cell-cycle-associated genes prioritized branched-chain amino acid transaminase 1 (BCAT1), whose high expression was associated with adverse outcomes in both primary and relapsed EwS. Functional genomics analyses revealed that BCAT1 is transcriptionally regulated by the EwS-specific EWSR1::FLI1 fusion oncoprotein through a distal enhancer-like GGAA microsatellite. Using prime-edited endogenous alleles and isogenic cell models, we found that disrupting BCAT1 redox-active CXXC motif increased sensitivity to oxidative stress and impaired recovery from it. Motif disruption also caused chromosome-segregation defects and DNA damage, reduced three-dimensional growth, and suppressed tumor formation and metastasis in vivo. By contrast, catalytic inactivation had limited effects. Although acute BCAT1 protein depletion reduced proliferation and tumor formation, constitutive BCAT1 knockout cells remained viable in culture and reduced tumor formation less than motif disruption. Mechanistically, CXXC motif disruption reduced casein kinase 2 (CK2) activity and increased Aurora kinase B (AURKB) activity, whereas BCAT1 degradation left CK2 activity unchanged and reduced AURKB activity. The enhanced sensitivity of CXXC-mutant cells to AURKB inhibition suggests a therapeutic vulnerability that could be exploited in BCAT1-wild-type EwS cells through combined CK2 and AURKB inhibition with silmitasertib and barasertib, increasing maximal growth inhibition and lowering the barasertib concentration required to suppress proliferation. Collectively, these findings reveal a mitotic vulnerability associated with BCAT1 redox-motif disruption that is not fully reproduced by protein loss and can be therapeutically exploited using clinically evaluated CK2 and AURKB inhibitors.

papers.title: CLOVER: Chemical-gene LLM benchmark for obtaining valid entity relationships for the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD)
papers.abstract: Objective: The Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) provides expert-curated chemical-gene interactions about environmental exposure effects on human diseases. Existing automated relation extraction systems are typically restricted to 3-10 interaction types and operate on abstracts only. We introduce CLOVER, a systematic benchmark for evaluating large language models (LLMs) on full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction using CTD-defined chemical-gene interaction terminology. The framework is designed to support 47 base interactions with directional modifiers (increase, decrease, affects), yielding 136 possible supported interaction classes. Evaluation is restricted to the subset of classes represented in the selected articles. Methods: CLOVER processes 50 full-text PubMed Central articles (1,563 sections) with PubTator and CTD integration. The pipeline consists of four stages: (1) LLM Extraction with one-shot and few-shot prompting; (2) LLM Validation to confirm and revise interactions; (3) Rule-based Refinement of extracted interactions to standardize terminology and eliminate errors; and (4) Human Review for expert oversight. We benchmark four LLMs (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, Claude-Sonnet-4.5, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) and compare against a naive baseline that applies unstructured prompting directly to full-text PDFs. Results: The naive baseline achieves only 13% recall and 36% precision. Refinement significantly enhances performance by eliminating unsupported interactions. Under strict limitations, Claude-Sonnet-4.5 alone achieves 72% recall and 61% precision, and Claude with self-validation achieves 74% recall and 49% precision compared to CTD. Of the 136 supported interaction classes, 17 were represented in our evaluation. Conclusion: To our knowledge, CLOVER establishes the first benchmark for full-text chemical-gene interaction extraction aligned with CTD. Our findings demonstrate that CLOVER achieves workable metrics for CTD-aligned curation relative to minimal whole-PDF prompting. This study addresses only a fraction of the content manually curated in CTD; considerably more work is needed to advance LLM-based tools to determine the extent to which these tools can approximate the full capacity of manual curation at CTD.

papers.title: A scalable method for preparation and long-term preservation of tea leaf plant-derived vesicles in tissue regeneration and drug encapsulation
papers.abstract: Plant-derived vesicles (PDVs) are emerging as sustainable nanotherapeutic platforms, although challenges regarding isolation, scalability, biological activity, drug loading, and storage stability hinder their biomedical translation. This study aimed to optimize PDV production, exploring different sources to assess the one with greater translation potential, in terms of for yield and purity. To that end, PDVs from tea and red cabbage leaves, as well as ginger and turmeric roots were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), comparing both methodologies. Tea provided the highest vesicle yield and purity, with SEC outperforming ultracentrifugation in reducing soluble protein contamination. SEC isolated tea leaf-derived PDVs (Tea PDVs) were therefore further optimization using scalable fast protein liquid chromatography. Proteomic characterization showed enrichment in hydrolases, which could be related to an inherent capacity to induce tissue remodelling. Hence, regenerative potential was tested in vitro on mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and endothelial cells (HAECs). Firstly, Tea PDVs showed no cytotoxicity in MSCs and HAECs, even at high concentrations. Importantly, they significantly attenuated staurosporine-induced MSC death and promoted endothelial wound closure and capillary-like network formation, supporting their regenerative potential. Drug delivery potential was also assayed using quercetin, as a proof-of-concept drug. Saponin-mediated permeabilization significantly improved quercetin loading compared with passive incubation. Another important hurdle towards clinical translation, is determination of the ideal storage conditions for PDVs, which is still missing. To address this, we performed a six-months storage study at -80 C, analysing different cryopreservatives. The results showed that PBS alone caused substantial particle loss and increased vesicle size, whereas HEPES + trehalose-, sucrose-, and trehalose + human albumin-containing cryoprotective formulations preserved vesicle size and mitigated particle loss, facilitating long-term stability. Overall, these findings identify Tea PDVs as promising biocompatible nanocarriers with intrinsic regenerative properties. The optimized isolation, drug-loading, and preservation strategies provide a foundation for further development of plant-based nanotherapeutics targeting tissue regeneration and drug delivery applications in regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Hitchhiker bias can distort inference of pathogen severity and pathogen-pathogen interactions from symptom-based surveillance: A modeling study
papers.abstract: Symptom-based infectious disease surveillance, which infers pathogen circulation by testing individuals who seek care for clinical symptoms, is widely used in public health but can distort our understanding of pathogen dynamics. Detecting a pathogen in a hospitalized patient does not establish that it caused the hospitalization. When a mildly pathogenic virus is detected in patients hospitalized because of a co-infecting, more pathogenic virus, the hospitalization can be wrongly attributed to the mild virus, a mechanism we term hitchhiker bias. Building on the aetiology-attribution literature, we couple this misattribution to a two-pathogen SEIR model with explicit co-infection and multiplex observation, and ask how an unmodeled incidental-detection pathway is absorbed into the parameters estimated by transmission models. We show that the relative inflation of observed hospitalizations is governed by the ratio of the two viruses hospitalization probabilities and by the fraction of mild-virus infections that are co-infections. In simulation-estimation experiments, ignoring the hitchhiker pathway overestimated the hospitalization probability of the mild virus about 3-fold under partial and 7-fold under complete epidemic overlap, with credible intervals that excluded the true value. In the absence of biological interaction, it also overestimated the mild viruss reproduction number and generated spurious inhibition under partial overlap, and generated spurious facilitation under complete overlap. When the viruses truly interacted, the bias in the estimated interaction depended on epidemic overlap: a true inhibition appeared stronger under partial overlap but was reversed into weak facilitation under complete overlap, and a true facilitation appeared stronger. Explicitly modeling the hitchhiker pathway recovered hospitalization probabilities and interaction strengths when the observation model was correctly specified. These results highlight the importance of separating pathogen-attributable hospitalization from incidental detection when drawing epidemiological inferences from symptom-based surveillance. Author summaryWhen people are sick enough to go to hospital, doctors can now test them for many viruses at once. It is easy to assume that any virus found in a patient helped cause the hospital stay. But that is not always true. A patient can carry a mild virus that causes few symptoms and also a more serious virus that is the real reason they were admitted. The mild virus is then found only because the patient happened to be tested for the serious one. We call this "hitchhiker bias". Using computer simulations of two viruses spreading through a population, we found that this can make a mild virus look more serious than it really is. It can also make the two viruses look as if they help each other spread when they do not. The effect is strongest when both viruses are spreading at the same time. In our simulations, a method that took this into account gave far more accurate answers.

papers.title: The unedited acceptance rate: a review-fidelity metric for human-in-the-loop clinical AI
papers.abstract: Objective. Guidance for large language model (LLM) drafting in clinical care relies on human review, yet review is rarely measured as a control. We aimed to define computable measures of review fidelity, establish which a deployed system can compute, and pre-specify their first analysis. Materials and Methods. For a multi-agent clinical system in routine use at one private London outpatient clinic, we defined acceptance coverage, attribution completeness, the unedited acceptance rate (UAR), a bounded normalized edit distance, availability latency and an unedited fast-approval rate (UFA). We checked each measure against the system's code and database structure at a fixed commit on four approval routes and pre-specified a prospective 12-week analysis. Results. The UAR equals the mass at zero of the edit-distance distribution, and availability latency bounds reading time from above only. Clinical documentation keeps draft and signed text with a recorded signer, so the core measures are computable there. Help-desk edit telemetry is written only when the agent's version has been stored. The WhatsApp agent route records no edit signal, and its approver need not be named. No route records when a draft is opened. Documentation accept events were not written before a change committed on November 16, 2026. Model-generated content, including live voice-agent speech, also reaches patients without approval. No measured values are reported. Discussion. Acceptance alone cannot separate accurate drafts from approval without reading, and three of four routes cannot yet support the family. Conclusion. Review fidelity can be specified as telemetry at the approval event. Validation against missed errors is required.

papers.title: Machine Learning Prediction of Autism ADOS-2 Calibrated Severity Scores Using Genetic and Behavioral Features
papers.abstract: Background: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized by social communication difficulties and restricted, repetitive behaviors. While machine learning has been widely applied in autism research, few studies have predicted continuous autism severity measures such as the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule Calibrated Severity Score (ADOS CSS). We evaluated behavioral and genetic predictors of ADOS CSS across ADOS modules. Methods: Participants from the Simons Simplex Collection who completed ADOS Modules 1, 2, or 3 were included. Behavioral questionnaire data and gene-level measures of loss-of-function intolerance (pLI, LOEUF) and brain-expression specificity (pExt) were used to train 12 machine learning models separately for each module. Performance was evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), Pearson correlation (r), and SHAP analyses. Results: Ensemble-based models achieved the strongest performance across modules. In Module 1, adding genetic predictors improved Random Forest performance (MAE 1.189 to 1.051; r 0.204 to 0.340). Module 2 achieved the highest overall performance, with XGBoost reaching r {approx} 0.49 and MAE = 1.010. SHAP analyses showed that genetic predictors contributed most strongly in Module 1, whereas predictions for Module 3 were driven primarily by verbal, behavioral, and social-cognitive features. Conclusions: Integrating genetic and behavioral features improved ADOS CSS prediction, particularly in children with limited expressive language. Genetic information was most informative in Module 1, while behavioral and social-cognitive measures became increasingly important in later developmental stages, consistent with evidence that genetic burden is more strongly associated with greater developmental impairment.

papers.title: Viral discovery using untargeted metagenomics and complementary proteomics in plasma cell-rich virus-like tubulointerstitial nephritis after kidney transplantation
papers.abstract: Background Kidney allograft biopsies may show plasma cell-rich tubulointerstitial inflammation and tubular epithelial changes suggestive of viral infection despite negative routine testing for known viruses. Whether this plasma cell-rich virus-like tubulointerstitial nephritis (PCR-TIN) is associated with an unrecognized viral agent is unknown. Methods We retrospectively identified 57 kidney allograft biopsies with a plasma cell-rich tubulointerstitial phenotype. Frozen tissue from 34 biopsies and matched urine from 14 cases underwent virus discovery cDNA-amplified fragment length polymorphism next-generation sequencing (VIDISCA-NGS). BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy (BKPyVAN) tissue served as a positive control for viral detection in renal tissue. Data-independent acquisition parallel accumulation-serial fragmentation liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry was used to evaluate the feasibility of detecting BK polyomavirus peptides. In an exploratory secondary analysis, host-protein abundance and Hallmark pathway enrichment were compared among 11 PCR-TIN, 91 other rejection, and 20 BKPyVAN biopsies. Results In positive-control experiments, VIDISCA-NGS detected BK polyomavirus at 13 of 216,879 reads (0.006%) and, after DNase treatment, at 5 of 81,614 reads (0.006%). Across the 34 PCR-TIN biopsies, 3,751,011 reads were generated (mean, 110,324 per biopsy). Sporadic low-level anelloviruses and Merkel cell polyomavirus reads (<10 reads per positive specimen) were detected in five and four biopsies, respectively, but no consistent candidate pathogenic viral agent was identified. Similarly, no candidate pathogenic viral agent associated with PCR-TIN was identified among 409,563 reads from the 14 matched urine samples (mean, 29,255 per sample). Proteomic interrogation did not detect BK polyomavirus peptides even in proven BKPyVAN, rendering this approach technically inconclusive for viral detection in PCR-TIN. Six proteins were significantly more abundant in PCR-TIN than in other rejection, whereas none differed significantly between PCR-TIN and BKPyVAN. Compared with both groups, PCR-TIN showed enrichment of epithelial-mesenchymal transition, interferon-response, allograft-rejection, inflammatory, and unfolded-protein-response programs, whereas oxidative phosphorylation and several metabolic pathways were enriched in the comparator groups. Conclusion Repeated VIDISCA-NGS of kidney tissue and matched urine did not identify a candidate pathogenic viral agent associated with PCR-TIN. These findings make a prevalent virus detectable by this workflow less likely but do not exclude low-abundance, focal, transient, or methodologically inaccessible infection. Exploratory host proteomics identified inflammatory, cellular-stress, and tissue-remodeling programs associated with PCR-TIN, but these findings characterize the accompanying host response, not its cause.

papers.title: Fine-tuned encoders, generative large language models and typed decisions for classifying findings in chest CT reports: paired English-Japanese internal testing and external testing on naturally written Japanese reports
papers.abstract: PurposeTo compare fine-tuned encoders, generative large language models (LLMs) and typed decisions (per-finding yes/no questions answered with a probability) for classifying 18 findings in chest CT reports, and to identify when typed decisions help. MethodsThis retrospective study used public data. The internal test set comprised 150 CT-RATE reports with paired Japanese translations at three quality levels; the external test set, 243 naturally written Japanese reports with human annotations (RR-Findings). We compared ModernBERT encoders fine-tuned on 20,444 reports, generative LLMs (gpt-6-luna, Qwen3.8-27B, MedGemma), and typed decisions with Jev, the Decisions API and Qwen. Thresholds fixed on 450 development reports were applied unchanged externally. The primary metric was micro-F1; case-level paired bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for 11 internal comparisons. ResultsEncoders were best internally (English 0.9853; radiologist-checked Japanese 0.9576) and exceeded Jev (differences 0.0367, 95% CI 0.0258-0.0484; 0.0336, 0.0215-0.0464). Externally, Jev (0.8844) lay within the encoder seed range (0.8656-0.9144), exceeded the three generative conditions tested externally (best 0.8564) and the Decisions API (0.8177), and had the smallest internal-to-external decrease (-0.0396). An encoder trained on 2,044 reports reached 0.8226 externally. Typed-versus-generated differences changed direction across models and test sets. At a fixed threshold of 0.5, Jev fell to 0.7753 externally. ConclusionFine-tuned encoders performed best with ample in-distribution labels. Although threshold-dependent, Jev, with thresholds fitted on only 450 labeled reports, fell within the encoder seed range externally and exceeded the generative LLMs and an encoder trained on 2,044 reports, making it an option when labels are scarce.

papers.title: Genome-resolved quantitative metagenomics of nontuberculous mycobacteria and their associated phages and plasmids in chloraminated drinking water
papers.abstract: Nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) are opportunistic pathogens of growing concern in drinking water, yet the phages and plasmids associated with them remain uncharacterized. We used genome-resolved quantitative metagenomics in three buildings on a chloraminated distribution system. Total bacterial metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) and viral population concentrations averaged 8.41x10^7 and 8.00x10^8 copies/L, respectively, while the total concentration of the seven NTM MAGs averaged 4.01x10^5 copies/L. Converging genomic evidence supported the identification of four viral MAGs (vMAGs) as putative mycobacteriophages. Three of these vMAGs encoded lysin B, a mycolylarabinogalactan esterase that cleaves the linkage between mycolic acids and arabinogalactan in the cell envelope, and three encoded a WhiB-family transcriptional regulator. NTM concentrations were highest at the site with the lowest bacterial and viral diversity. Combined four-vMAG concentrations were positively associated with total NTM concentrations within sites, although the association across all nine samples was not significant. NTM plasmids carried ESX secretion and metal efflux genes at higher proportions than NTM chromosomes. NTM carried more steroid degradation genes than co-occurring Actinomycetota. These findings reveal site-specific NTM-phage concentration relationships and identify phage- and plasmid-associated functions with potential implications for NTM-phage interactions and environmental adaptation.

papers.title: Equity gaps in the genetic diagnosis of monogenic cardiomyopathy: an intersectional analysis of race and gender in the All of Us Research Program
